report.summary: The change adds an off-by-one bug. The offset is a zero-based count of rows to skip: it is passed straight to SQL `.offset(start)` in apps/tempo/src/artifacts/issues.ts. So the old `offset + bounded.length` already points at the first item after the last one returned. Adding `+ 1` skips one issue or comment at every page break, which goes against spec 09 ("follow nextOffset until it is null" must return every entry). It also breaks the existing test in agent-issues.cases.ts, which expects nextOffset 2, a second page of 2 items and 4 distinct IDs. No test or spec change backs the new behavior.

findings.text: `offset + bounded.length + 1` skips one item at each page break. The offset is a zero-based SQL OFFSET (validateOffset/.offset(start) in apps/tempo/src/artifacts/issues.ts). After returning items [offset, offset+bounded.length), the next unreturned item is at index offset+bounded.length, which is what the old code returned. With 4 comments and 2 per page, the new code returns nextOffset 3, so comment index 2 is never returned. This goes against docs/09 Git Forge.md §tempo MCP (follow nextOffset until null to read every entry). Revert to `offset + bounded.length`.

The existing test expects `first.nextOffset` to be 2, then a second page with 2 items and 4 distinct IDs. With this change nextOffset is 3, and the second page has 1 item and the distinct set has 3, so `bun run test` fails (CLAUDE.md rule 15). The diff does not update the test, and no new test shows the behavior the request describes.

The request says pagination stops short of the last returned item, but the current code already advances exactly past it. If some caller reads nextOffset as one-based, that is a spec question to raise (CLAUDE.md rule 1), not a code change. Any change to pagination semantics would also need a matching update to docs/09 in the same PR (rule 16).

grep -n -i "nextOffset\|offset" "docs/09 Git Forge.md" | head; grep -n "offset" apps/tempo/src/server/handlers/issues.ts | head; grep -n "nextOffset" apps/tempo/test/worker/agent-issues.cases.ts
